title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights for travelers
lede: United Airlines will block third-party AI agents from booking flights for travelers, citing the risk of shared account logins and federal rules that need a person for steps such as check-in.

points: The airline says handing credentials to an assistant can expose personal data and lead to unintended purchases, account changes or MileagePlus redemptions.
It points to rules such as passengers confirming in person that their bags hold no banned items.
United will restrict agents on its own sites and, indirectly, through travel agencies and aggregators.
Analyst Henry Harteveldt reads it as United keeping control of booking and avoiding the cost of bot-driven searches.
Southwest has gone the other way, making its flights viewable to ChatGPT users.

sections.text: Agents that act on a user's account depend on sites letting them in. A large airline refusing on security and regulatory grounds is an early sign that agent builders will need sanctioned integrations, not logins.
